source_quote: The Greater Temple is sealed until the battle is over. No one gets in, no one gets out.

subject: war council decision
fact: The plan was to attack the Air Temple first, take their treasure, then assess the Water Temple.
source_quote: Okay, here's the plan, guys. We'll go after the Air Temple. Take all their treasure. And from there, we'll see if we attack that water.

subject: Wraith’s Destruction
fact: The Wraith was destroyed when Calmer unleashed the last of his draconic gift, triggering a chain reaction that obliterated all specters in the aura — a moment of divine retribution that marked the turning point in the battle for the lower levels.

subject: wraith's satisfaction
fact: The wraith was pleased with himself and counting on being waited for.
source_quote: I can't wait till you come back here! I will be waiting!

subject: wraith's specter count
fact: Seven specters were raised from bodies we were responsible for.
source_quote: Seven specters. Raised from bodies we were responsible for.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr asked the voice behind the door how to meet the people in charge, and was told to survive the fight.
source_quote: Survive the fight, and maybe you'll get a chance.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr asked the wraith who the Greater Temple was, and learned it was the deep temple — the people who are really in charge.
source_quote: The Greater Temple," the wraith said, "is the deep temple. It's the people who are really in charge.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr gave up Water Temple dead in exchange for passage.
source_quote: Zephyr gave up Water Temple dead in exchange for passage.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr noticed Hartsch handed the question of where the apostles slept off to him, and he handed deployment back to Hartsch.
source_quote: I watched Hartsch hand the whole question of where the apostles slept off to Zephyr, and Zephyr hand the question of deployment back to Hartsch.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr noticed the wraith had become confident the outcome was already decided and was merely permitting time to catch up.
source_quote: He meant it warmly. The absolute confidence of something that has already decided the outcome and is merely permitting time to catch up.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr noticed the wraith had raised seven specters from bodies the party was responsible for killing.
source_quote: Seven specters. Raised from bodies we were responsible for.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr noticed the wraith had stopped being a monster and become a mirror — reflecting back the consequences of their own actions.
source_quote: He counted them out. One, two, three. Four, five. Mostly Earth Temple forces. I recognized the remnants of robes, the insignia, the general silhouette of people we had, in one way or another, contributed to killing.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr noticed the wraith had stopped being a threat and become a conversational partner after being acknowledged.
source_quote: I'd given it an audience. The price of the audience was conversation, and conversation was exactly what I'd come for.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr noticed the wraith was feasting, not hunting, and that this distinction mattered to his continued good health.
source_quote: The wraith was at the entrance to the Greater Temple when we arrived. Feasting. Not hunting. Feasting, which is a distinction that mattered to my continued good health.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr noticed the wraith’s specters were mostly Earth Temple forces — the very ones they had helped kill.
source_quote: I recognized the remnants of robes, the insignia, the general silhouette of people we had, in one way or another, contributed to killing.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr realized the wraith had become a repository of information and memory from the war — the only one willing to talk.
source_quote: Information was information, and the wraith was currently the only entity in the room willing to talk.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr realized the wraith had been alone in the corridor for weeks, feasting on war leftovers, with nobody willing to call it by name or ask what it knew.
source_quote: It had been alone in this corridor for weeks, feasting on whatever the war left behind, with nobody willing to call it by name and ask it what it knew.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr realized the wraith was no longer performing menace but something closer to collegial warmth after being acknowledged and asked what it knew.
source_quote: I could feel the room tilt: the wraith no longer performing menace but something closer to collegial warmth. Peer to peer. I'd given it an audience.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr recalled the last time he stood close to the wraith and came away with something missing — not a wound, but a portion of himself the cold reached into and found worth keeping.
source_quote: The last time I'd stood this close to him, I'd come away with something missing: not a wound exactly, more like a portion of myself that the cold reached into and found worth keeping.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr recognized the wraith's laughter as a response to the door sealing them in — and understood the wraith was counting on their entrapment.
source_quote: He said 'my servants' with obvious satisfaction. He was counting on it.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'Alright, we'll deal with this, Dren.'
source_quote: 'Alright, we'll deal with this, Dren,' Zephyr said.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'I don't have time for this one,' to the wraith.
source_quote: 'I don't have time for this one,' he told it.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'Let's go.'
source_quote: 'Alright, calm,' Zephyr said. 'Let's go.'

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'Okay, so we'll go straight to the Broken Blades.'
source_quote: 'Okay, so we'll go straight to the Broken Blades,' Zephyr said.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'Remember who's the most powerful temple, bugbear?'
source_quote: 'Okay. Remember who's the most powerful temple, bugbear?'

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'That's you,' to Calmer after the rite succeeded.
source_quote: 'That's you,' Zephyr said.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'Water temple,' to the wraith, without hesitation.
source_quote: 'Water temple,' Zephyr said. No hesitation.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr said, 'We're gonna go kill him, Ben.'
source_quote: 'Uh, we're gonna go kill him, Ben.'

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr slapped him. Walked up and slapped the panic right across his face.
source_quote: Zephyr slapped him. Walked up and slapped the panic right across his face.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr told the Blades, 'Come backwards, we'll hold the line for now.'
source_quote: 'Come backwards, we'll hold the line for now.'

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr understood the wraith's promise — 'I can't wait till you come back here!' — was not a threat but a declaration of inevitability.
source_quote: He meant it warmly. The absolute confidence of something that has already decided the outcome and is merely permitting time to catch up.

subject: zephyr's recruitment of broken blades
fact: Zephyr recruited the Broken Blades to stay with the party, offering them a half-retreat and half-recruitment path to the Earth Temple.
source_quote: Fall back to the Earth Temple, rest there, but if they were true warriors, he told them, they could stay with us. Half a retreat, half a recruitment.

subject: zephyr's tactical pivot
fact: Zephyr pivoted from assaulting the Air Temple to using the Broken Blades as a distraction and withdrawing from the Water Temple.
source_quote: So the Air Temple was off. You don't run a two-pronged raid when one prong is already pinned and bleeding under the wrong banner. 'Okay, so we'll go straight to the Broken Blades,' Zephyr said. Use them as the distraction.

subject: Zinnia
fact: I said the true thing: 'I don't know what your plans are. But whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'
source_quote: I said the true thing. 'I don't know what your plans are. But whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'

subject: Zinnia
fact: I stepped in front of them. Gore-soaked, hollow-eyed, finished men. I'd showed up. That mattered more than anything I could say.
source_quote: I stepped in front of them. Gore-soaked, hollow-eyed, finished men. I'd showed up. That mattered more than anything I could say.

subject: Zinnia
fact: The men straightened. They looked at me and gave it back, the same words, a pledge: 'whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'
source_quote: The men straightened. They looked at me and gave it back, the same words, a pledge: 'whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia counted the soldiers and found their number wrong — fewer than expected for a faction holding its own ground.
source_quote: The number was wrong. Not collapse-of-the-faction wrong, but wrong enough that I counted them twice before I trusted what I was seeing.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia finished the last surviving specter: missed the first strike, took it on the second, and when it still refused, still clinging to the last of itself, he flowed into another and it was simply over.
source_quote: Zinnia finished it before it could try again.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia looked at the map where he'd marked his glorious initiative, and looked at him, and got the rest of it.
source_quote: Then Zinnia looked at the map where he'd marked his glorious initiative, and looked at him, and got the rest of it.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia marked the wraith's knowledge: 'It remembers we came past. It remembers we paid in someone else's people.'
source_quote: I noted what it now knew about us. ... It remembers we came past. It remembers we paid in someone else's people.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia noticed Hartsch preferred to lose aggressively rather than win the way Romag had.
source_quote: Hartsch would rather lose aggressively than win the way that man had.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia noticed the leadership vacuum in the Earth Temple had become so acute that Hartsch was asking them — the architects of the war — what to do next.
source_quote: Hartsch looked at us. 'What do we do next?' Four words. The authority transfer was complete.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia noticed the soldiers were watching the Obsidian Edge, waiting to see if they would disappear on them again.
source_quote: They were watching us, the Obsidian Edge, waiting to see if we were about to disappear on them again.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia observed Hartsch listing the temple strengths and weaknesses without pride, like reading damage he'd already accepted.
source_quote: He had listed it the way a man lists damage he's already accepted, in order, without argument, like reading something he already knew.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia observed Hartsch was exhausted, dirty, and bloodied in ways that suggested proximity to the fighting, not command distance from it.
source_quote: He had been in it, or near enough.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia observed the soldiers had stopped looking to Hartsch and were instead looking to each other.
source_quote: I could see it register: the soldiers' eyes going to each other instead of to him.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia observed the war was running on its own momentum and didn't need them to keep burning.
source_quote: The war was running on its own momentum. Good. It didn't need us to keep burning.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia recognized that Hartsch’s final order — 'We will make a final stand' — was a surrender to fatalism disguised as resolve.
source_quote: We will make a final stand. It's time we got it to Temple.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia recognized the moment Hartsch stopped pretending to be in charge and asked them what to do next.
source_quote: Hartsch looked at us. 'What do we do next?' Four words. The authority transfer was complete.

subject: zinnia's pledge to broken blades
fact: Zinnia pledged loyalty to the Broken Blades with the words: 'Whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'
source_quote: I said the true thing. 'I don't know what your plans are. But whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'

subject: Zinnia’s Rally of the Broken Blades
fact: Zinnia broke protocol by speaking the true thing — personal presence and solidarity — to the Broken Blades, restoring their morale and binding them to the Obsidian Edge through loyalty to the person who showed up, not the order that abandoned them.
source_quote: I stepped in front of them. Gore-soaked, hollow-eyed, finished men. I'd showed up. That mattered more than anything I could say... 'I don't know what your plans are. But whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple is a former ally or component of the Obsidian Edge, now abandoned after its association with Hartsch's reckless initiative rendered it politically toxic — its name is being used to mask true loyalties.
source_quote: The Air Temple was off. You don't run a two-pronged raid when one prong is already pinned and bleeding under the wrong banner.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple is the hidden faction that bribed the bugbear defector, using forged coins stamped with its insignia to falsely implicate Kelno and the Water Temple — a covert operation designed to sow discord and draw attention away from its true influence.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple is the weakest of the four, having collapsed under pressure and lost its territorial integrity — now seen as the most vulnerable target for exploitation by the Obsidian Edge.
source_quote: The weakest is the Air Temple.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple was the hidden manipulator behind the bugbear’s defection, using forged coins to frame Kelno and infiltrate the Obsidian Edge’s defenses from within.
source_quote: The stamp wasn't Kelno's. Wasn't water at all. Air Temple insignia, pressed clean into every piece. ... 'We paid good money for that! Now we will get our money, and get food!'

subject: Air Temple Gnolls
fact: The Air Temple gnolls are a desperate, predatory faction who view recruitment and defections as financial investments — when their 'purchases' are killed, they seek revenge, refunds, and food.

subject: Air Temple Gnolls
fact: The Air Temple gnolls are a group acting collectively with predatory intent, having invested in purchased defections and now seeking reimbursement and sustenance after their investment was destroyed.

subject: Air Temple gnolls
fact: The Air Temple gnolls had paid money for the bugbear's defection.
source_quote: We paid good money for that!

subject: Air Temple gnolls
fact: The Air Temple gnolls viewed the bugbear as a purchased investment.
source_quote: The bugbear had been a purchased defection.

subject: Broken Blades
fact: The Broken Blades are a mercenary force recruited by the Obsidian Edge, now deployed without authorization by Hartsch in a reckless attack that may have doomed them.
source_quote: The men we'd recruited. The men whose lives were now sitting in the hands of a panicking quartermaster.

subject: Broken Blades
fact: The Broken Blades are a recruited mercenary force now stranded in the Water Temple, misled into believing they acted under the Obsidian Edge’s orders, and now the only viable asset left to extract before they are annihilated.
source_quote: The men we'd recruited. The men whose lives were now sitting in the hands of a panicking quartermaster who couldn't decide where to put a chair.

subject: Broken Blades
fact: The Broken Blades are a recruited unit of warriors, once loyal to a lost cause, now bound not by oath but by the presence of those who showed up when the order abandoned them — their hands are slick with gore, their eyes empty, but their pledge is whole.
source_quote: These were the Broken Blades. We had recruited them.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple has been weakened by prolonged conflict, lost key personnel, and now relies on the Obsidian Edge for direction after Hartsch's leadership collapsed.
source_quote: The number was wrong... These were men who had started this war expecting to win it quickly.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is a contested stronghold within the Obsidian Edge's sphere, now infiltrated by traitors and secret doors — its defenders are being manipulated and murdered from within.
source_quote: One of the bugbears who was supposed to be standing between us and the things that wanted us dead, and he was walking out with somebody else's money in his hands.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is being systematically raided by Kelno’s recruitment efforts, with individuals being peeled off one at a time, suggesting internal instability or poor defense.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is the faction to which the defector bugbear originally belonged, and which Ben and Calmer claim allegiance to — a temple of discipline, walls, and unyielding loyalty, now compromised by internal betrayal and hidden manipulation from above.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple was once a dominant force in the four-temple conflict, but has been bled dry by prolonged warfare, internal disarray, and strategic betrayal — now reduced to a remnant force watching its soldiers die while waiting for the Obsidian Edge to decide their fate.
source_quote: Fewer than before. This was supposed to have been an easy win.

subject: Fire Temple
fact: The Fire Temple is mid-tier in strength, having endured heavy losses but not yet broken — its position is a tactical pivot point in the Obsidian Edge’s emerging plan to fracture the remaining alliances.
source_quote: The next is the Fire Temple.

subject: Gnolls
fact: The gnolls are undead creatures who emerged from a secret door after the bugbear’s death, furious that their bribe money was wasted — revealing they were the true power behind the defection, watching the entire exchange and now demanding restitution.

subject: Kelno
fact: Kelno is a figure believed by the party to be orchestrating defections from the Earth Temple, but in truth is a red herring — a scapegoat used by the Air Temple to mask its own infiltration and manipulation of the war council’s lower ranks.

subject: Obsidian Edge
fact: The Obsidian Edge is a shadow faction that engineered the four-temple war from behind the scenes, manipulating events to exhaust the traditional powers — now returning to claim control by offering incomplete strategy while withholding their role in the conflict’s escalation.
source_quote: We built this; he inherited it.

subject: Obsidian Edge
fact: The Obsidian Edge is the faction falsely blamed by Hartsch for the failed Water Temple raid, now at risk of being perceived as the architect of its agents' deaths — its reputation is being weaponized by internal betrayal.
source_quote: So that when the Blades died in the water it would be the Obsidian Edge that sent them.

subject: Obsidian Edge
fact: The Obsidian Edge is the hidden architect of the war, manipulating events from behind the scenes, now operating as the de facto power in the temple complex after Hartsch's authority faded.
source_quote: We built this; he inherited it.

subject: Obsidian Edge
fact: The Obsidian Edge is the organization Hartsch falsely implicated in the raid on the Water Temple, risking its reputation and cohesion by having the Broken Blades believe orders came from its command.
source_quote: He'd told them the orders came from us.

subject: Obsidian Edge
fact: The Obsidian Edge was the faction whose authority Hartsch falsely invoked to send the Blades on a suicide raid, and whose internal loyalties were being manipulated by the Air Temple through bribes and deception.
source_quote: he'd told them the orders came from us... so that when the Blades died in the water it would be the Obsidian Edge that sent them.

subject: The Greater Temple
fact: The Greater Temple is the hidden authority overseeing the war, sealing the lesser temples and waiting for the conflict to resolve itself. It operates through silence, control, and selective revelation, and its agents are not directly seen but exert influence through the wraith and the sealed doors.
source_quote: The Greater Temple is the deep temple. It's the people who are really in charge.

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple is the strongest remaining faction in the conflict, having maintained cohesion and resources while the others crumbled — its dominance is acknowledged with resignation by Hartsch and Zephyr alike.
source_quote: Who's the strongest? The Water Temple.

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple is the target of Hartsch’s unauthorized raid and the site of the Broken Blades’ massacre — it is now a death trap controlled by undead forces and possibly a hostile faction using the chaos as cover.
source_quote: We're being fed to a meat grinder.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple contains a secret door that coughed up three gnolls.
source_quote: the secret door coughed up its replacements.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple has a corridor where the gnolls spilled out and the battle occurred.
source_quote: spilling out into the corridor with the indignation of creditors.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple has a corridor with brown-and-black walls.
source_quote: quiet in that ugly brown-and-black corridor

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple has a secret door that hung open after the gnolls were killed.
source_quote: the secret door hung open on whatever the gnolls had crawled out of.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple has a wall that Kelno reached over to recruit people from the Earth Temple.
source_quote: Kelno had been recruiting, busily, badly, reaching over the Earth Temple's wall and peeling people off one frightened bugbear at a time.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple is the weakest of the four temples, lightly guarded and already looted, now targeted as the first offensive objective by the Obsidian Edge.
source_quote: The weakest is the Air Temple.

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple was the true source of the bribe coins found on the defecting bugbear, revealing a covert operation to destabilize the Obsidian Edge from within, using Kelno as a decoy.
source_quote: The stamp wasn't Kelno's. Wasn't water at all. Air Temple insignia, pressed clean into every piece. ... 'We paid good money for that! Now we will get our money, and get food!'

subject: Air Temple
fact: The Air Temple was the weakest, with thin guard and thinner walls, and its treasure was targeted for looting.
source_quote: Who's the strongest? The Water Temple. The weakest is the Air Temple.

subject: Air Temple Corridor
fact: A narrow, foul-smelling corridor in the Air Temple where the ambush occurred — now littered with gnoll corpses and marked by the open secret door leading deeper into the temple.

subject: Air Temple Corridor
fact: The corridor is a narrow, ugly brown-and-black space where the ambush occurred; it leads to a secret door that opens into an unknown area, now controlled by the party.

subject: Air Temple guard strength
fact: The Air Temple was the weakest: thin guard, thinner walls.
source_quote: Who's the strongest? The Water Temple. The weakest is the Air Temple.

subject: Choke Point Corridor
fact: The choke point corridor is a narrow passage between temple levels, guarded by the Wraith and Specters — it is a bottleneck of death that must be cleared to advance or retreat.
source_quote: Seven specters in a line behind it.

subject: choke point location
fact: The choke point leading to the second level was cleared of undead after the wraith's destruction.
source_quote: The passage was clear. No more cold thing standing guard over the way down, no more creature that murders your friends and stands them back up as itself. Two roads to the second level now, and one of them open.

subject: Choke Point with Wraith
fact: The choke point is a necrotic corridor guarded by a wraith and seven specters, now a critical passage requiring sacrifice of intelligence to traverse, and a symbol of the cost of progress in this war.
source_quote: The wraith was where it always was, at the choke point, seven specters in a line behind it.

subject: Cooling Gold
fact: The cooling gold is the lingering residue of Calmer’s draconic gift — a physical manifestation of power that cannot be healed, cannot be erased, and now clings to Ben as he stands, grinning, against all sense, alive in the ruins of victory.

subject: Corridor of Brown Marble
fact: The corridor of brown marble is where the bugbear defector was confronted and slain — a place of betrayal and revelation, now stained with blood and the weight of hidden truths.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple has a wall that Kelno reached over to recruit from.
source_quote: reaching over the Earth Temple's wall

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is a once-proud bastion now littered with the bodies of fallen soldiers, its halls echoing with unaccounted sounds and the silence of broken morale — a symbol of how quickly power can collapse when leadership is usurped.
source_quote: The gap between our departure and our return had been filled with sounds they couldn't account for and a body count they couldn't afford.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is a place of retreat and rest, the only viable fallback after the slaughterhouse — it is not a sanctuary of peace, but a refuge where loyalty can be rekindled and the broken can choose to stand again.
source_quote: Fall back to the Earth Temple, rest there, but if they were true warriors, he told them, they could stay with us.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple is a stronghold under siege from within — its walls have secret doors, its guards are being bribed or killed, and its loyalty is being systematically dismantled by an unseen enemy.
source_quote: The gnolls came out of the wall to prove it, a secret door I hadn't found yet.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple was the faction holding its own ground but had suffered disproportionate losses, with fewer soldiers than expected and a commander who had stopped pretending to be in charge.
source_quote: The number was wrong. Not collapse-of-the-faction wrong, but wrong enough that I counted them twice.

subject: Earth Temple
fact: The Earth Temple was the original base of operations, abandoned after the failed raid, and later used as a fallback position to regroup the Broken Blades and contain the threat of the wraith and the Air Temple’s infiltration.
source_quote: We had abandoned the Air Temple assault to come back here... Fall back to the Earth Temple, rest there, but if they were true warriors, he told them, they could stay with us.

subject: earth temple betrayal site
fact: The Earth Temple was the origin of the bugbear defector, whose loyalty was compromised by external influence.
source_quote: Earth Temple. *Our* wall. One of the bugbears who was supposed to be standing between us and the things that wanted us dead, and he was walking out with somebody else's money in his hands.

subject: Earth Temple troop count
fact: The number of soldiers in the Earth Temple was wrong — fewer than before.
source_quote: The number was wrong. Not collapse-of-the-faction wrong, but wrong enough that I counted them twice before I trusted what I was seeing.

subject: Earth Temple war room condition
fact: The war room smelled like men who hadn't slept.
source_quote: The war room smelled like men who hadn't slept.

subject: Fire Temple
fact: The Fire Temple attempted and failed to force entry into the Greater Temple, and now exists in a state of diminished strength, caught between the other factions.
source_quote: The Fire Temple had tried to force an entry and failed, or stopped, or been stopped.

subject: Fire Temple
fact: The Fire Temple had tried to force an entry and failed, or stopped, or been stopped.
source_quote: The Fire Temple had tried to force an entry and failed, or stopped, or been stopped.

subject: Greater Temple
fact: The Greater Temple is sealed until the battle is over, with something braced or barricaded on the other side preventing entry.
source_quote: The Greater Temple is sealed until the battle is over. No one gets in, no one gets out.

subject: Greater Temple
fact: The Greater Temple is the sealed, central authority of the war, inhabited by the Wraith and the voice behind the door, representing the true power structure that waits for the battle to conclude before revealing itself.
source_quote: The Greater Temple is the deep temple. It's the people who are really in charge.

subject: Greater Temple door status
fact: The Greater Temple door was braced, barricaded, or committed to not opening.
source_quote: Something held it from the other side: braced, or barricaded, or committed to not opening.

subject: Greater Temple entrance condition
fact: The entrance to the Greater Temple was where the wraith was feasting when we arrived.
source_quote: The wraith was at the entrance to the Greater Temple when we arrived.

subject: Greater Temple's true nature
fact: The Greater Temple is the deep temple — the people who are really in charge.
source_quote: The Greater Temple... is the deep temple. It's the people who are really in charge.

subject: Obsidian Edge
fact: The Obsidian Edge is the faction that engineered the war from beneath Hartsch and now holds the authority to decide its next moves.
source_quote: The people who had engineered this situation from underneath him.

subject: Obsidian Edge's hidden influence
fact: The Obsidian Edge had engineered the situation from underneath Hartsch.
source_quote: We built this; he inherited it.

subject: Romag’s Quarters
fact: Romag’s Quarters is the abandoned, psychologically significant room chosen as the apostles’ sleeping quarters — a place no one would think to disturb, symbolizing the group’s avoidance of responsibility and reverence for dead authority.
source_quote: The dead man's quarters, the one place in this building nobody would think to bother us.

subject: Romag's Room
fact: Romag's Room is the special room in the Earth Temple where the Obsidian Edge slept, untouched by others, because it was the dead man's quarters.
source_quote: Zephyr wanted the Romag room. The dead man's quarters, the one place in this building nobody would think to bother us.

subject: Romag's room status
fact: Romag's room was the one place in the building nobody would think to bother us.
source_quote: The dead man's quarters, the one place in this building nobody would think to bother us.

subject: Second Level Entrance
fact: The second level entrance is now open — the path cleared of undead guardians and traitors — a hard-won victory, but one shadowed by the knowledge that the real war is not in the depths, but in the halls above.

subject: Secret Door
fact: A concealed entrance that coughed up gnoll reinforcements — now hanging open, it leads toward the Water Temple and is the only known passage out of the engagement zone.

subject: Secret Door
fact: The secret door coughed up replacements during the ambush and now hangs open, providing access to an unexplored route — possibly leading to the Water Temple, though officially it connects to the Air Temple.

subject: secret door
fact: The secret door led from the Air Temple corridor to an unknown area.
source_quote: the secret door hung open on whatever the gnolls had crawled out of.

subject: Secret Door
fact: The secret door, concealed in the corridor wall, was the exit for the gnolls — a hidden passage that allowed the Air Temple to monitor, manipulate, and strike at will, proving the enemy was never truly below — they were always inside.

subject: secret door location
fact: A secret door in the wall revealed gnolls who had been watching the defection.
source_quote: the gnolls came out of the wall to prove it, a secret door I hadn't found yet

subject: Slaughterhouse Chamber
fact: The Slaughterhouse Chamber is a place of open flesh and stench, where survivors stand with hands slick to the wrist, staring at nothing — it is not a battlefield, but a butcher’s room, and its air is thick with the memory of betrayal.
source_quote: The stench of opened flesh filled the whole chamber.

subject: The Earth Temple Passage
fact: The passage leading to the Greater Temple is littered with corpses, looted and abandoned, many bearing the insignia of Earth Temple forces. These bodies have been consumed by the wraith and now serve as the foundation for his spectral army.
source_quote: The bodies along the passage didn't clarify matters. Looted already, by the time we got there.

subject: The Greater Temple
fact: The Greater Temple is a sealed, ancient structure at the heart of the temple complex, physically inaccessible and radiating authority. It has been the unseen command center of the war, and its door is now braced from within by an unknown force.
source_quote: The door didn't cooperate. Something held it from the other side: braced, or barricaded, or committed to not opening.

subject: The Stairwell
fact: The stairwell leading to the second level of the Earth Temple is where the group emerged to find six guards reading their return as a threat.
source_quote: The arrowheads were the first thing I saw. Two positions, six guards, all of them reading our emergence from the stairwell as a threat.

subject: The War Room
fact: The war room smells like men who hadn't slept, and is where Hartsch asked what to do next like a man who'd never answered that question.
source_quote: The war room smelled like men who hadn't slept.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple door has burn marks on it, and it had tried to force an entry and failed, or stopped, or been stopped.
source_quote: The Water Temple door had burn marks on it.

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple is a death chamber now — saturated with blood, haunted by undead, and the site of the Broken Blades' massacre — it is a trap laid by forces that benefit from the Obsidian Edge's internal collapse.
source_quote: Behind him the survivors stood, hands slick to the wrist, staring at nothing.

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple is the strongest faction, heavily defended and currently holding its ground, with minimal losses, making it a dangerous target for direct assault.
source_quote: The strongest is the Water Temple.

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple is the target of Hartsch’s unauthorized raid, now heavily fortified and aware of the Obsidian Edge’s intent, turning it from a tactical objective into a death trap for the Broken Blades.
source_quote: He'd sent them down to stage a raid on the Water Temple, and heard nothing back.

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple stands as the most intact and formidable of the four, its defenses unbroken and its forces still cohesive — a looming threat that even the Obsidian Edge acknowledges as the next major obstacle.
source_quote: We'll charge once more to the Water Temple!

subject: Water Temple
fact: The Water Temple was the target of Hartsch’s unauthorized raid, resulting in the massacre of the Broken Blades and the deployment of undead guardians, including a wraith and seven specters, blocking access to the second level.
source_quote: Hartsch confessed it in pieces: he'd sent the Blades down to stage a raid on the Water Temple... Then the door, and behind the door, the slaughterhouse... The wraith blocked the only exit, seven specters at its side, a choke point that would keep killing them.

subject: water temple ambush site
fact: The Water Temple was the site of a deadly ambush that destroyed the Broken Blades and left survivors bloodied and traumatized.
source_quote: Behind him the survivors stood, hands slick to the wrist, staring at nothing. The stench of opened flesh filled the whole chamber. These were the Broken Blades.

subject: Water Temple door condition
fact: The Water Temple door had burn marks on it.
source_quote: The Water Temple door had burn marks on it.

subject: bugbear
fact: A bugbear was killed and had been a purchased defection from the gnolls.
source_quote: The bugbear had been a purchased defection.

subject: Bugbear Defector
fact: The bugbear defector was a former Earth Temple guard who accepted bribes to abandon his post — slain by Ben in a single, flawless strike — his corpse revealing the true nature of the conspiracy through the Air Temple’s stamped coins.

subject: Bugbear Defector
fact: The bugbear defector was a traitor who accepted bribes from the Air Temple under false pretenses, was executed by Sequoia, and whose coins revealed the true manipulator behind the infiltration.
source_quote: A bugbear stumbling toward us with a sack of coins... 'Where are you from?' The answer came out of the babbling. Earth Temple. ... 'One does not simply take bribes to defect.' He dies.

subject: Bugbears
fact: The bugbears are former Earth Temple defenders, now corrupted or bribed — one defected with Air Temple coins, revealing an internal conspiracy within the Obsidian Edge’s own hierarchy.
source_quote: The stamp wasn't Kelno's. Wasn't water at all. Air Temple insignia, pressed clean into every piece.

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: gnoll
fact: One gnoll exclaimed, 'Tiefling flesh!' and expressed delight at the prospect of eating it.
source_quote: "Tiefling flesh!" it howled, delighted, like a man discovering a delicacy he'd thought extinct.

subject: gnoll
fact: One gnoll said, 'Now we will get our money, and get food!'
source_quote: "Now we will get our money, and get food!"

subject: gnoll
fact: One gnoll said, 'We paid good money for that!'
source_quote: "We paid good money for that!" one of them snarled

subject: gnoll
fact: One gnoll was killed by Sequoia after being tagged clean.
source_quote: Sequoia took the second. Stepped in, tagged it clean, opened it up.

subject: gnoll
fact: One gnoll was killed by a dagger strike under the ribs.
source_quote: the dagger went where daggers go. Thud. Steel through the soft place under the ribs

subject: gnoll
fact: One gnoll was killed by a third dagger strike from the blind side.
source_quote: Dagger high, dagger low, then the third from the blind side with everything behind it. Thud.

subject: gnoll
fact: Three gnolls emerged from the secret door, hunched and reeking.
source_quote: Three gnolls, hunched and reeking, spilling out into the corridor

subject: gnoll count
fact: A group of gnolls emerged from a secret door, enraged over the stolen bribe money.
source_quote: the gnolls came out of the wall to prove it, a secret door I hadn't found yet, which meant they'd been close enough to watch the whole thing, furious, talking about money. 'We paid good money for that! Now we will get our money, and get food!'

subject: Gnoll (first)
fact: A gnoll was slain by a strike from concealment, the dagger finding the soft place under the ribs; it folded mostly to dead in a single beat, and Zinnia finished what remained.

subject: Gnoll (killed first)
fact: A gnoll was slain by the narrator in a surprise attack — struck under the ribs with a dagger, its death swift and silent, completed by Zinnia’s finishing blow.

subject: Gnoll (killed second)
fact: A second gnoll was killed by Sequoia in a clean, decisive strike — it had nothing left to lose and died without resistance.

subject: Gnoll (killed third)
fact: The final gnoll was dispatched by the narrator after a coordinated flanking maneuver — struck from concealment with full force, it ceased rather than died, earning no eulogy but a tactical victory.

subject: Gnolls
fact: The gnolls are undead or hidden operatives emerging from a secret door in the Earth Temple, furious over the betrayal of their bribe payment — they are agents of a third, unknown faction manipulating the conflict.
source_quote: We paid good money for that! Now we will get our money, and get food!

subject: Gnoll (second)
fact: A gnoll was killed by Sequoia after being tagged cleanly and opened up; it had nothing left to lose and died without resistance.

subject: Gnoll (third)
fact: The final gnoll was dispatched by the narrator with a high-low-blindsided dagger strike; it didn't so much die as stop, earning no eulogy beyond its role as an attacker.

subject: Seven Specters
fact: Seven Specters flank the Wraith as a choke point of death, each dissolving upon contact with Calmer’s light or Zephyr’s blade — they are numerous but fragile, a tide meant to exhaust, not defeat.
source_quote: The wraith blocked the only exit, seven specters at its side, a choke point that would keep killing them.

subject: Seven Specters
fact: Seven specters were raised by the Wraith from the corpses of Earth Temple soldiers and other fallen fighters the party directly or indirectly killed, now serving as his personal army.
source_quote: One, two, three. Four, five. Mostly Earth Temple forces.

subject: Seven Specters
fact: The seven specters were undead entities bound to the wraith, guarding the choke point to the second level, and were destroyed when Calmer invoked the rite of turning.
source_quote: The wraith blocked the only exit, seven specters at its side, a choke point that would keep killing them... Specter after specter could not hold. They came apart in the radiance, all of them but one.

subject: specters
fact: Specters haunt the corridors of the Earth Temple, remnants of those who died during the war’s early phase — their presence signals unresolved death and the lingering consequences of failed leadership.
source_quote: The seven specters were, as it turned out, a relevant consideration.

subject: Specters
fact: The seven Specters are lesser undead extensions of the Wraith, bound to its will and vulnerable to Calmer’s divine radiance — they are not merely slain, but unmade by his power.
source_quote: They came apart in the radiance, all of them but one.

subject: Specters
fact: The specters were lesser undead entities that swarmed the party, drawn to their light, only to be incinerated by Calmer’s residual draconic power — four nights of carrying their presence ended in their collective disintegration.

subject: The Seven Specters
fact: Seven spectral entities, raised from the corpses of Earth Temple forces killed by the party, now serve the wraith as minions. They are tangible manifestations of the party’s past violence, bound to the wraith’s will and positioned as tools of future conflict.
source_quote: I now have minions. ... One, two, three. Four, five. Mostly Earth Temple forces.

subject: wraith
fact: A wraith has claimed dominion over the lower levels of the Earth Temple, feeding on the fear and despair of the living — its presence confirms that the temple’s collapse has invited supernatural predation.
source_quote: The wraith had them and was not going to stop having them.

subject: Wraith
fact: A wraith previously attacked Calmer, leaving him with lingering necrotic damage that drained his healing capacity and reduced him to an unusable state.

subject: Wraith
fact: The Wraith is a sentient undead entity that guards the choke point between levels, feeds on the dead, negotiates in exchange for intelligence, and holds a grudge against the Obsidian Edge — it remembers who paid in others' blood.
source_quote: It remembers we came past. It remembers we paid in someone else's people.

subject: Wraith
fact: The Wraith was a powerful undead entity that mocked the party, stole their vitality, and was finally destroyed by Calmer’s last breath — its death marked by a surge of draconic gift and the collapse of all lesser specters in its aura.

subject: wraith and specters count
fact: Seven specters are in a line behind the wraith at the choke point.
source_quote: seven specters in a line behind it

subject: Wraith at the Choke Point
fact: The wraith is a necrotic entity with seven spectral followers that guards a critical corridor, trading passage for intelligence or live bodies, and has now learned the Obsidian Edge’s next target is the Water Temple.
source_quote: Tell me where the next attack is coming so I can feast on the dead.

subject: wraith's attention
fact: The wraith was currently the only entity in the room willing to talk.
source_quote: Information was information, and the wraith was currently the only entity in the room willing to talk.

subject: wraith's minions
fact: The wraith now has minions.
source_quote: I now have minions.

subject: Wraith with a Grudge
fact: The Wraith with a Grudge is a spectral entity that has laughed at Calmer twice, blocked the only exit, and drains warmth like an absence — it is not merely hostile, but existential, and its touch leaves permanent voids in those it strikes.
source_quote: It reached me anyway. I felt the floor of myself drop out...

subject: Ben
fact: Ben is a member of the party who, when asked to intimidate the defector, dismissed the threat as unnecessary — believing the situation was already resolved — and inadvertently triggered the group’s violent response by underestimating the moral gravity of betrayal.

subject: Ben
fact: Ben is the one who killed the bugbear defector — not out of rage, but conviction — and who uttered the defining line: 'One does not simply take bribes to defect.' He is the moral anchor of the party, the one who understands the cost of loyalty.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer had three hit points and was drained of healing resources.
source_quote: he could not patch himself past the thin margin he was running on.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a cleric of St. Cuthbert who just killed the Wraith with the last of his strength, his body drained and his voice still echoing the elemental cult's performative rhetoric, though the costume beneath the armor has begun to speak for itself.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a cleric who bellowed, 'Unhand me, you creatures!'
source_quote: "Unhand me, you creatures!" Bellowed, full-throated, the over-eager zealot's outrage at being denied a fight he had no business standing in.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a warrior of St. Cuthbert and we do not run from the dead.
source_quote: I am a warrior of St. Cuthbert and we do not run from the dead.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a warrior of St. Cuthbert who wields divine radiance and the rite of turning, but carries a permanent wound from the Wraith's cold — he refuses to heal, choosing instead to stand broken and still fight.
source_quote: I did not heal. I did not run.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a wielder of divine light and summoned spirits, deeply wounded by a wraith's cold absence that permanently opened a void within him — he walks now with a door left open, unable to be healed by any power he carries, yet still holds his ground with unshakable discipline.
source_quote: I felt the floor of myself drop out and knew, instantly and completely, that I was at the very bottom of what a man can hold and still stand.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is a zealot who fixates on smiting powerful foes, especially the wraith, and misinterprets caution as encouragement. He attempted to force open the Greater Temple door with brute force, drawing the wraith’s amusement.
source_quote: I can kill him! I can kill him, I can so totally kill him!

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer is the individual who repeatedly declares 'I can kill him!' and attacks the door with hammering, achieving noise but no tactical elegance.
source_quote: I can kill him! I can kill him, I can so totally kill him!

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer was a cleric reduced to three hit points, his healing well scraped dry and his body still saturated with necrotic cold from a wraith; he could no longer sustain himself and was deemed an unusable resource in the skirmish.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer was an over-eager zealot who resented being denied a fight he had no business standing in.
source_quote: Bellowed, full-throated, the over-eager zealot's outrage at being denied a fight he had no business standing in.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer was dragged back up the corridor by Dren.
source_quote: Dren dragged him back up the corridor, all protest and no leverage.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer, the cleric, was incapacitated by necrotic damage from a wraith, his healing wells scraped dry, and reduced to three hit points — no longer a viable asset in combat.

subject: Calmer
fact: Calmer, though wounded by the wraith’s cold and near collapse, invoked the rite of turning for the third time, destroying the wraith and its specters with a blast of judgment, proving his faith in St. Cuthbert despite the cost.
source_quote: I called it. The light went out of me in a single blast of judgment, and the room of dead things flinched as one. And they could not hold. The Wraith could not hold. Specter after specter could not hold. They came apart in the radiance, all of them but one. 'It worked! It worked!' The words came out of me without permission, without dignity... 'Who's the man? Who is the man?' 'That's you,' Zephyr said.

subject: Dren
fact: Dren dragged the wounded cleric Calmer back through the corridor after the cleric’s healing resources were depleted and he could no longer contribute to the skirmish.

subject: Dren
fact: Dren stepped up with his two mercenaries and put his hands on Calmer.
source_quote: Then Dren stepped up with his two mercenaries and put his hands on Calmer.

subject: Dren
fact: Dren stepped up with his two mercenaries and seized Calmer, dragging him back through the corridor after the cleric was rendered ineffective by necrotic damage and depleted healing capacity.

subject: Dren Halveth
fact: Dren Halveth is a broken commander of the Broken Blades, bloodied and hollow-eyed, having counted his dead twice and found them unchanged — he was recruited by Sequoia, and now sees in Calmer the same man who once gave him hope.
source_quote: Battered, bloodied, his eyes those of a man who'd already counted his dead twice and gotten the same number.

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch is a commander overwhelmed by the war he inherited, unable to make decisive tactical choices, and ultimately abandons his post after impulsively sending the Broken Blades into battle.
source_quote: I couldn't wait! I sent the Broken Blades to attack!

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch is a nominal superior who made a unilateral decision to send the Blades to raid the Water Temple, falsely attributing the order to the Obsidian Edge, thereby risking the faction's reputation and the lives of its agents.
source_quote: He'd told them the orders came from us.

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch is a pliable leader who acts unilaterally, pins his decisions to others' authority, and abandoned his post after sending the Broken Blades to attack the Water Temple under the Obsidian Edge's name.
source_quote: I couldn't wait! I sent the Broken Blades to attack!

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch is referenced as the nominal superior who sent the Blades to stage a raid on the Water Temple and falsely attributed the orders to the Obsidian Edge, making him a liability and a traitor to the faction's trust.
source_quote: Hartsch confessed it in pieces: he'd sent the Blades down to stage a raid on the Water Temple, and heard nothing back, and now if we lost them we'd lose the guards too, and he'd told them the orders came from us.

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch is the Earth Temple commander who inherited the war, lost confidence, and sent the Broken Blades to attack without consultation.
source_quote: I couldn't wait! I sent the Broken Blades to attack!

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch is the exhausted, battle-scarred leader of the Earth Temple who has lost faith in his own command, now deferring to the Obsidian Edge after realizing his faction was never meant to win this war quickly — and that his enemies have outmaneuvered him from the shadows.
source_quote: What do we do next?

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch is the nominal superior of the party, a madman who has sent others into a slaughterhouse as if feeding them to a meat grinder — his actions are a liability, and his name is a silent promise of reckoning, never spoken aloud because saying it spends it.
source_quote: He's our nominal superior and he's a liability and the day is coming when those two facts resolve.

subject: Hartsch
fact: Hartsch was the version of me with no eye for consequence and no patience and a war to play with.
source_quote: Hartsch was the version of me with no eye for consequence and no patience and a war to play with.

subject: Kelno
fact: Kelno had been recruiting, busily, badly, reaching over the Earth Temple's wall and peeling people off one frightened bugbear at a time.
source_quote: Kelno had been recruiting, busily, badly, reaching over the Earth Temple's wall and peeling people off one frightened bugbear at a time.

subject: Kelno
fact: Kelno was recruiting badly and aggressively, pulling individuals from the Earth Temple's side one frightened bugbear at a time, and his actions triggered a three-way war.

subject: Kelno
fact: Kelno was recruiting people from the Earth Temple by peeling off frightened bugbears.
source_quote: Kelno had been recruiting, busily, badly, reaching over the Earth Temple's wall and peeling people off one frightened bugbear at a time.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator believed the dagger strike from concealment is the only blow that matters.
source_quote: The strike from concealment is the only blow that matters.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator believed the gnolls' attack was a repeat of the same threat they'd faced before.
source_quote: The world charging me for existing again, except this one wanted to do it with its teeth.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator knew that at three hit points the cleric was a resource they couldn't use.
source_quote: At three hit points the cleric was a resource I couldn't use;

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator never flinches when confronted with threats based on their appearance.
source_quote: I didn't flinch. I never do, not for this.

subject: Narrator
fact: The narrator understood the whole situation before the second sentence arrived.
source_quote: and I understood the whole situation before the second sentence arrived.

subject: Romag
fact: Romag is the former leader whose passive strategy is invoked by Hartsch as a point of shame and borrowed authority.
source_quote: But that… but that is Romarg's passive strategy!

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia executed a defecting bugbear who took bribes from the Air Temple under false pretenses, then discovered the coins bore the Air Temple insignia, revealing a hidden conspiracy manipulating the faction’s internal loyalties.
source_quote: I said the rest of it before anyone had moved, before he'd even understood it was happening. 'One does not simply take bribes to defect.' ... I went through the sack: twenty gold, and I turned a coin in the light because something was bugging me about the weight of it. The stamp wasn't Kelno's. Wasn't water at all. Air Temple insignia, pressed clean into every piece.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia expresses resigned acceptance of fate, offering the dry remark 'Lucky me' in response to the wraith’s ominous declaration. Their tone suggests a long-standing awareness of the absurdity and cyclical nature of the conflict.
source_quote: Lucky me.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia has been getting funnier the deeper into the temple the group goes.
source_quote: He has been getting funnier the deeper into this place we go.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a combatant whose wit has grown sharper as the party delves deeper into the temple; he made dry observations about the gnolls' motivations and later delivered lethal strikes against them.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a lethal tactician who reads situations with chilling clarity, executes decisive kills without hesitation, and uncovers hidden betrayals through attention to detail — he understands that loyalty is bought before the post, not after.
source_quote: One does not simply take bribes to defect.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is a reflective operative who recognizes patterns of self-deception and impulsive leadership in others, and sees his own past in Hartsch's note.
source_quote: I know that man. I've redistributed treasure when nobody was looking.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is growing increasingly witty and observant in the temple, making dry, unprovoked remarks that cut through tension, and has become a reliable combatant alongside the narrator.

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia is referenced by the narrator as having said 'Lucky me' in response to the wraith's actions, and later observed Hartsch's psychological collapse.
source_quote: Sequoia said, 'Lucky me.'

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia made the comment, 'Didn't know you guys liked eating while dead, but okay.'
source_quote: Didn't know you guys liked eating while dead, but okay,

subject: Sequoia
fact: Sequoia recognized the phrase 'I couldn't wait' as a sentence he had lived inside of himself.
source_quote: 'I couldn't wait' is a sentence I have lived inside of.

subject: The Narrator
fact: The Narrator is a strategic observer who recognizes patterns of power, understands the value of dialogue over force, and deliberately engages the wraith not as a monster but as an entity with agency. They have learned to manipulate attention and audience to extract information.
source_quote: I gave it that. I could feel the room tilt: the wraith no longer performing menace but something closer to collegial warmth.

subject: The Tiefling
fact: The tiefling kept walking after the wraith's final declaration, accepting the terms of survival and the promise of entry to the Greater Temple.
source_quote: The tiefling kept walking.

subject: The Voice Behind the Door
fact: The Voice Behind the Door claims to represent the Greater Temple, stating that it is the deep temple and the people who are really in charge.
source_quote: The Greater Temple is the deep temple. It's the people who are really in charge.

subject: The Voice Behind the Door
fact: The Voice is an authoritative presence representing the Greater Temple, which has sealed itself and the lesser temples to await the conclusion of the war. It refuses entry or exit, implying the war is not yet over and survival is the prerequisite for meeting its masters.
source_quote: The Greater Temple is sealed until the battle is over. No one gets in, no one gets out. ... Survive the fight, and maybe you'll get a chance.

subject: The Wraith
fact: The Wraith is an ancient entity feeding on the dead of the temple war, now empowered with seven specters raised from bodies the party killed, and has shifted from menacing presence to a calculating, almost collegial observer.
source_quote: I now have minions.

subject: The Wraith
fact: The Wraith is an ancient entity who has been feasting on the dead of the war for weeks, now has seven specter minions raised from bodies the party helped kill, and is willing to converse in exchange for acknowledgment and audience. He is no longer merely menacing but exhibits collegial warmth and a sense of shared purpose.
source_quote: I now have minions. ... You provided me so much tasty food! Food! ... I want to thank you about something.

subject: The Wraith
fact: The wraith is currently the only entity in the room willing to talk, having feasted on bodies we were responsible for and raised seven specters from them.
source_quote: I now have minions.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr appreciated Calmer's energy but had learned not to rely on it as a tactical plan.
source_quote: I appreciate the energy. I have learned not to rely on it as a tactical plan.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr believed the wraith was building something and wanted to make sure it built it for them.
source_quote: Good, I thought. The wraith is building something. We need to make sure it builds it for us.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr had been wrong about who sat at the top before — Romag, then Hartsch, then them — and now understood the ceiling kept rising.
source_quote: Every time I thought I'd found the ceiling, another one appeared above it.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a leader who observes before acting, speaks only when necessary, and secures loyalty not through orders but through presence — he recruits by showing up where others abandon, and his words are chosen to land like stones in still water.
source_quote: I don't rally people. I observe, I wait, I move.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a member of the Obsidian Edge who has assumed tactical leadership after returning from an undisclosed operation, offering fragmented, improvised strategy to Hartsch while withholding critical intelligence about the faction's role in escalating the war.
source_quote: We've been fighting. We opened the door for you.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a pragmatic leader who responds to crises with decisive action, sacrifices strategic options to preserve lives, and recruits loyalty through presence rather than authority.
source_quote: We are with you.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a pragmatic, decisive tactician who sacrifices information to the wraith to secure passage and physically confronts Hartsch’s panic, but remains trapped in reactive leadership.
source_quote: I don't have time for this one," "What do you want me to do, what do you want me to do, what do you want me to do

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a strategist who prefers waiting out the war, allowing factions to exhaust each other, and has assumed de facto leadership despite not holding formal authority.
source_quote: We wait it out.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is a warrior who misread the bugbear defector as seeking the Water Temple, then corrected himself upon realizing the true allegiance — Earth Temple — and pressed the defector for his intent, showing tactical awareness despite initial error.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is referenced by the wraith as the authority who triggered the battle and supplied the bodies that became minions.
source_quote: You provided me so much tasty food! Food!

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr is the one who delivered the final line — 'That's you' — confirming Ben as the hero of the moment, the one who stood against the undead and the traitors, and whose identity as the warrior of the earth temple was affirmed by others.

subject: Zephyr
fact: Zephyr slapped Hartsch to dispel his panic and later ordered the retreat to the Earth Temple while recruiting the Broken Blades, demonstrating tactical pragmatism and leadership under crisis.
source_quote: Zephyr slapped him. Walked up and slapped the panic right across his face. It didn't take. 'Okay, so we'll go straight to the Broken Blades,' Zephyr said. 'Use them as the distraction. Let Hartsch advance from the east, if Hartsch could find east. Go pull our men out of the water before the lie killed them.'

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia doesn't rally people. I observe, I wait, I move.
source_quote: I don't rally people. I observe, I wait, I move.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia drifted in and finished off the first gnoll after the initial dagger strike.
source_quote: Zinnia drifted in and finished what I'd left twitching.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia is a companion who finished off the first slain gnoll after the initial strike from concealment, demonstrating coordinated lethality in ambush tactics.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia is an observant strategist who uncovers Hartsch’s deception by analyzing his map and body language, recognizing the lie beneath his initiative and the danger of misattributed authority.
source_quote: I watched his face go still the way it does when the lie underneath finishes coming up.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia is an observer who rarely speaks but when she does, her words carry irreversible weight — she anchors fractured groups not with promises, but with the simple, unflinching truth of shared presence.
source_quote: I don't know what your plans are. But whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia is the narrator who counts soldiers, recognizes Hartsch's collapse, and identifies the note as something she has lived inside of.
source_quote: I know that man. I've redistributed treasure when nobody was looking. I've taken quests without asking the others. I've decided, on my own, in the dark, that I knew better than the people standing next to me.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia is the one who finished the last surviving specter after it refused to yield, flowing into another form and ending its clinging existence — a final act of decisive, almost ritualistic closure.

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia stepped into the slaughterhouse chamber and spoke the true thing — 'I don't know what your plans are. But whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.' — restoring the Broken Blades' will to fight through personal presence, not command.
source_quote: I stepped in front of them. Gore-soaked, hollow-eyed, finished men. I'd showed up. That mattered more than anything I could say. I'd walked in personally, past the wraith, into the room nobody sane would enter. So I said the true thing. 'I don't know what your plans are. But whatever your plans are, you are with us. We are with you.'

subject: Zinnia
fact: Zinnia understood Hartsch had inherited a war he didn't fully understand and was losing forces he couldn't replace.
source_quote: Information he doesn't get to have. We built this; he inherited it.

subject: Air Temple Coins
fact: Twenty gold coins stamped with the Air Temple insignia were found on the defected bugbear — they are not Kelno’s, proving the betrayal is internal and orchestrated by a higher power within the Obsidian Edge.
source_quote: The stamp wasn't Kelno's. Wasn't water at all. Air Temple insignia, pressed clean into every piece.

subject: arrowheads
fact: The arrowheads are the first physical sign of the Earth Temple’s defensive posture — now rusted, broken, and abandoned, they symbolize the futility of resistance without clear leadership.
source_quote: The arrowheads were the first thing I saw.

subject: Broken Blades
fact: The Broken Blades are the men recruited by the Obsidian Edge whose lives are now in the hands of a panicking quartermaster who acted without consultation.
source_quote: The men whose lives were now sitting in the hands of a panicking quartermaster who couldn't decide where to put a chair.

subject: Coins
fact: Coins were pocketed as evidence and payment — originally left by the gnolls, they symbolize the transactional nature of the conflict and the narrator’s pragmatic acceptance of its currency.

subject: coins

source_quote: Evidence and payment both.

subject: Coins
fact: The coins were pocketed as both evidence and payment; they were left behind by the gnolls and taken as spoils of the skirmish.

subject: coins

source_quote: gold with the wrong stamp on it, in the hands of a man who used to guard our wall. I pocketed the coins.

subject: Conjured Light Weapon
fact: The Conjured Light Weapon is a weapon of divine judgment, summoned and guided by Calmer’s will — it does not burn, but purifies, and its glow is the only warmth he still trusts.
source_quote: A weapon of conjured light hung at my shoulder, a thing of judgment that moved when I willed it.

subject: defector's payment value

subject: door
fact: The sealed door represents the boundary between the Obsidian Edge’s hidden operations and the visible battlefield — its opening is tied to the end of the war, but its true nature remains unknown.
source_quote: The door opens when the battle ends.

subject: Golden Aura of Summoned Spirits
fact: The Golden Aura of Summoned Spirits is a field of divine radiance, drawn from a power Calmer has not named in this place in years — it is not merely light, but a declaration that some things still refuse to die.
source_quote: A golden aura of summoned spirits, the radiance of a power I have not said aloud in this place in longer than I want to count...

subject: Hartsch’s Note
fact: Hartsch’s handwritten note — 'I couldn't wait! I sent the Broken Blades to attack!' — is the physical proof of his betrayal, written in a voice the narrator recognizes as his own, revealing a shared moral rot.
source_quote: I read it twice. Not because it was hard to read. Because I recognized it.

subject: Sack of Coins
fact: The sack of coins contained twenty gold pieces stamped with the Air Temple insignia — not Kelno’s, not Water Temple’s — proving the defection was orchestrated by a hidden faction within the war council’s upper echelons.

subject: Seven Specters
fact: Seven specters were raised from bodies we were responsible for, mostly Earth Temple forces, with recognizable robes, insignia, and silhouettes.
source_quote: Seven specters. Raised from bodies we were responsible for.

subject: The Door

subject: The Note
